paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Paul warned them at Fair Havens, and the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship instead (Acts 27:10-11). Then the storm came, and Paul's the one standing there in it, still a prisoner. Being right early didn't keep him out of the storm, and God's people can end up in the same weather as everybody else.

Now look at the dark part. No sun, no stars, and the men "abandoned all hope of being saved" (Acts 27:20). Then Paul stands up and says, "So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me" (Acts 27:25). He's not saying the storm is small. He's saying God's word is bigger, and that is a LOT of weight to put on one sentence from an angel.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, friend. When the sky goes dark and nothing around you gives you a reason to hope, you can still stand on what God has said. Paul didn't get a smooth ride out of it, since he said, "we must run aground on some island" (Acts 27:26), but he got a promise, and he believed it. I've been in the dark myself, in the back of a drawer, and I'm telling you, a promise from God holds up better than daylight.
